column1: # SPEC-REGISTRY.tsv — where every acceptance spec actually runs.
# Enforced by test/acceptance-spec-coverage.bats (CI stage 1c). Adding a spec
# to this directory without adding a row here is a stage-1c failure, and so is
# a row whose claim disagrees with playwright.config.ts, the Makefile, or
# scripts/ci/vm-pipeline.sh.
# Commit d9d1d2f rewrote a test in smoke.spec.ts to assert the Collusion &
# Access page carries no page-specific background. Nothing enforced it: at that
# point smoke.spec.ts appeared in no CI stage and no make target, so the
# assertion could regress silently and forever. It was not the only one — of 15
# specs on disk, CI ran exactly one.
# Worse, four specs matched no `testMatch` in playwright.config.ts at all, so
# they ran nowhere, not even under a bare `make acceptance-test`. Playwright
# does not warn about a spec no project claims; it simply reports a smaller
# total. `bunx playwright test --list` on 978dfea says "70 tests in 12 files"
# against 16 files on disk, and nothing draws attention to the missing four.
# This is the same defect class as the dashboard vitest suite (fixed by CI
# stage 1b) and as the missing junit reporter documented in
# playwright.config.ts: a missing input degrades to nothing rather than to an
# error. The suite passes; it just proves less than the reader believes.
# TESTING.md already described this coverage in prose, and had already drifted:
# it says "68 tests across 9 specs, in four projects" while the config now has
# six projects and Playwright reports 70 tests in 12 files. Prose cannot fail a
# build. Every column below is cross-checked against the artefact that actually
# decides, in both directions, so a stale row is as loud as a missing one.
#   spec     Filename in this directory. Must exist; every *.spec.ts here must
#            appear exactly once.
#   runner   Where it runs automatically. One of:
#              ci:<stage>      a run_stage in scripts/ci/vm-pipeline.sh. The
#                              guard asserts that stage really names the spec.
#              make:<target>   a Makefile target. The guard asserts the target
#                              exists and that its recipe names the spec.
#              suite-only      matches a playwright.config.ts project, so a
#                              bare `make acceptance-test` runs it, but no CI
#                              stage and no dedicated target does.
#              unwired         matches NO project `testMatch`. Runs nowhere at
#                              all — not in CI, not via any target, not under
#                              `make acceptance-test`. The guard asserts this
#                              in both directions, so a spec cannot be marked
#                              unwired once it is wired, or stay marked
#                              suite-only after being dropped from the config.
#   reason   Required for everything except ci:*. Why it is not in a CI lane.
#            "it just isn't" is not a reason; name the blocking precondition,
#            because that sentence is the work item for wiring it in later.
# Tab-separated. Comments start with #. Order is alphabetical by spec.
#spec
afm-frontend.spec.ts
column3: Every test is behind guards.afmDeployed(); the CI lane never runs `make demo-k8s-afm-up`, so all 11 would SKIP. A stage of 11 skips is a green light that proves nothing, which is worse than an absent stage because it reads as coverage.

column1: afm-integration.spec.ts
column3: Same guards.afmDeployed() precondition as afm-frontend: 9 tests, all SKIP without the k8s-afm slice. Wire in only alongside deploying that slice in the lane.

column1: cluster.spec.ts
column3: Probes Grafana (13000), Archivista (18082) and the Olly portal (18080) — three services the CI lane does not deploy, and three port-forwards the TEST-1 branch of scripts/acceptance-test.sh does not create. TESTING.md's 2026-07-26 baseline records 4 of its 8 tests failing purely on service availability.

column1: credential-lifecycle.spec.ts
column3: Both tests test.skip() unless the live estate already holds an enrolled/active agent with a UUID-shaped agent_registry id. A freshly built CI cluster has none, so this contributes 2 skips. It needs a seeding step before it can mean anything in a lane.

column1: dashboard-journey.spec.ts
column3: Targets the Estate 95 win95 console at http://127.0.0.1:8675 (`make console`), a different application from the Signal Loom dashboard every other spec drives. It needs no cluster and no gateway, so it does not belong in any of the current projects — it wants a project of its own with `make console` as its precondition.

column1: rbac-analysis.spec.ts
column3: Behind guards.afmDeployed(). One test, SKIP without the k8s-afm slice.

column1: rbac-explorer.spec.ts
column3: Behind guards.afmDeployed(). Ten tests, all SKIP without the k8s-afm slice.

column1: signalloom-login.spec.ts
column3: Three of its four tests re-prove Dex login/logout, which stage 8 already covers via signalloom-test-1.spec.ts's Dex contracts; the fourth needs AFM. Cheap, and the best candidate for the next stage — but adding it today buys duplicate coverage rather than new coverage.

column1: signalloom-test-1.spec.ts
smoke.spec.ts
supercred-evidence-lifecycle.spec.ts
column3: Its project sets a 30-minute test timeout. CI_STAGE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is 900, so a passing run would be killed mid-flight and reported as a stage failure. It also drives instructor phases that mutate one shared cluster, which is why its project sets retries:0.

column1: supercred-live-pages.spec.ts
column3: Needs the SuperCred demo to have been driven first, and needs the storageState the setup project writes. Adding it to the `smoke` project would silently run it unauthenticated — playwright.config.ts documents exactly that trap. It needs its own project with dependencies:["setup"].

column1: supercred-page.spec.ts
column3: Seeds the superadmin flag before app boot and needs the SuperCred demo deployed. Same storageState problem as supercred-live-pages: the `smoke` project would run it logged out.

column1: supercred-two-window.spec.ts
column3: Drives two browser contexts against a demo that mutates one shared cluster, and its project sets a 15-minute timeout — at or above the 900s CI stage cap, so CI would kill a healthy run. retries:0 for the same mutation reason, so a single flake fails the lane outright.

column1: supercred-ui-lifecycle.spec.ts
column3: 30-minute project timeout against the 900s CI stage cap, same as supercred-evidence-lifecycle. It runs all five phases, resets, then reruns them — the longest single test in the repo.
